lessons.title: Eid
lessons.goal: Greet people at Eid and talk about Eid customs.
grammar: locative / genitive of ঈদ: ঈদে 'at Eid', ঈদের দিন 'on Eid day'
lessons.tip:
Bangladesh celebrates two Eids: *Eid-ul-Fitr*, at the end of Ramadan, and *Eid-ul-Adha*, the festival of sacrifice, about two months later. Their dates follow the lunar calendar and move about 11 days earlier each year. Greet with **ঈদ মোবারক!**; the reply is the same.

On Eid morning people go to the Eid prayer (**ঈদের নামাজ**), wear **নতুন** (new) clothes and visit relatives. At Eid-ul-Fitr almost every home serves **সেমাই** (sweet milky vermicelli); at Eid-ul-Adha, families who can afford it sacrifice an animal and share the meat. Children greet elders with *salam* and get **সালামি** (Eid money): **আপু, সালামি দাও!** 'Apu, give me Eid money!'

Endings: *-e* = 'at', *-er* = 'of':

- **ঈদে আমরা গ্রামে যাই** — 'At Eid we go to the village'
- **ঈদের দিন সকালে** — 'on the morning of Eid day'

Eid is a public holiday (**ছুটি**), and millions leave Dhaka for their home villages.

sentences.en: At Eid we go to the village.
alt: We go to our village for Eid.

sentences.en: We have a holiday at Eid.
alt: At Eid we have a holiday.
There is a holiday at Eid.
Sister, give me my Eid money.

sentences.en: I will buy new clothes for Eid.
alt: I'll buy a new shirt for Eid.

sentences.bn: ঈদের দিন সকালে আমরা নামাজ পড়ি।
sentences.tr: ider din shokale amra namaj pori.
alt: On the morning of Eid we pray.

lessons.title: Ramadan & iftar
lessons.goal: Talk about fasting, sehri and iftar.
lessons.tip:
During **রমজান** (Ramadan), the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, most Bangladeshi Muslims fast from dawn to sunset, with no food or drink. Bengali says **রোজা রাখি**, literally 'I keep the fast'. It's the same verb you met in the bazaar (**কম রাখেন!**): **আমি রোজা রাখি** 'I fast', **আপনি কি রোজা রাখেন?** 'Do you fast?'

The day is framed by two meals: **সেহরি** before dawn and **ইফতার** at sunset. Many people break the fast with a **খেজুর** (date). A classic Dhaka iftar also has *chhola* (spiced chickpeas), *peyaju* (lentil-and-onion fritters), *beguni* (aubergine fritters) and *jilapi*.

Endings to notice: **রমজানে** 'in Ramadan', **ইফতারে** 'at iftar'. **ইফতার** also pairs with **করি** 'do': **আমি এখনো ইফতার করিনি** 'I haven't had iftar yet'.

Being invited to iftar is a warm gesture of friendship, and non-Muslim friends are welcome too. Asking **আপনি কি রোজা রাখেন?** is polite, but it is a personal question, so don't press. Ramadan ends with *Eid-ul-Fitr* (Lesson 1).

sentences.bn: আমি সেহরি খাই, তারপর নামাজ পড়ি।
sentences.tr: ami sehri khai, tarpor namaj pori.
sentences.en: I eat sehri, then I pray.
Iftar is at our home today.
alt: Today there's iftar at our house.

sentences.en: It's the month of Ramadan now.

alt: I haven't broken my fast yet.

lessons.title: Pohela Boishakh
grammar: আজ পহেলা বৈশাখ 'today is Pohela Boishakh'
lessons.tip:
**পহেলা বৈশাখ**, the first day of the month of Boishakh, is the Bengali New Year. In Bangladesh it falls on **14 April**, and people of every religion celebrate it together. Greet everyone with **শুভ নববর্ষ!** 'Happy New Year!'

Traditions:

- red and white clothes (often a white sari with a red border)
- **আলপনা** patterns painted on floors and streets
- a **মেলা** (fair) with crafts, toys and snacks
- in Dhaka, songs at sunrise and a big, colourful street procession
- **পান্তা ভাত** (rice soaked overnight in water) with fried ইলিশ
- shopkeepers open a new account book (*halkhata*) and offer sweets

**শুভ** + occasion is a common pattern: **শুভ নববর্ষ**, and later *shubho jonmodin* 'happy birthday'. (**শুভ সকাল** 'good morning' is mostly for messages.)

**মেলা** 'fair' → **মেলায়** 'to / at the fair': **তুমি কি মেলায় যাবে?** 'Will you go to the fair?'

**Kolkata:** **পয়লা বৈশাখ** (*poyla boishakh*), on 14 or 15 April.

sentences.en: Pohela Boishakh is the Bengali New Year.

sentences.bn: আমরা পান্তা ভাত আর ইলিশ খাই।
sentences.tr: amra panta bhat ar ilish khai.
sentences.en: We eat panta bhat and hilsa.
alt: We eat soaked rice and hilsa.

sentences.en: Will you go to the fair?

alt: The floor art is very beautiful.

sentences.en: I will buy a red sari.

lessons.title: Puja
lessons.goal: Talk about Durga Puja and greet Hindu friends.
grammar: শুভ বিজয়া — greeting after Durga Puja
lessons.tip:
About 8% of Bangladeshis are Hindu, and **দুর্গাপূজা** (*durgapuja*) is their biggest **উৎসব** (festival). It falls in autumn (September or October) and lasts several days. Temporary pavilions (*mondop*) each hold a clay **প্রতিমা**, an image of the goddess Durga, and people of all faiths come to see them.

On the last day, **বিজয়া** (*Bijoya Doshomi*, a public holiday in Bangladesh), the images are immersed in a river or pond. Afterwards people greet each other with **শুভ বিজয়া** and share sweets. With Hindu friends, **নমস্কার** is the natural hello.

**পূজা** means 'worship' as well as the festival. Endings: **পূজায়** 'at Puja', **মন্দিরে** 'to / at the temple'.

A popular saying: *dhormo jar jar, utshob shobar*, 'religion is each person's own; festivals belong to everyone'. **ঈদ আর পূজা আমাদের উৎসব** 'Eid and Puja are our festivals.'

**Kolkata:** spoken **পুজো** (*pujo*), **দুর্গাপুজো**; Durga Puja is West Bengal's biggest festival.

sentences.en: Durga Puja is a big festival of the Hindus.
alt: Durga Puja is the Hindus' big festival.

sentences.en: At Puja we go to the temple.
alt: During Puja we go to the temple.

sentences.en: I will buy a new sari for Puja.
Eid and Puja are our festivals.

lessons.title: Ekushe & national days
lessons.goal: Understand Language Martyrs' Day, Victory Day and Independence Day.
grammar: X দিবস 'X day'; দিবসে 'on the day'
lessons.tip:
On **21 February 1952**, police in Dhaka opened fire on students and others demanding that **বাংলা** be a state language of Pakistan (which then included today's Bangladesh). Several were killed. Every year on **একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি**, also called **শহীদ দিবস** (Martyrs' Day), people walk barefoot to the **শহীদ মিনার** from midnight on to lay flowers, singing *Amar bhaiyer rokte rangano Ekushe February* ('the 21st of February, reddened with my brother's blood'). Since 2000 the world also marks it as UNESCO's **International Mother Language Day** (**মাতৃভাষা** = mother tongue).

Two more national days mark the 1971 Liberation War. Both are public holidays (**ছুটি**):

- **স্বাধীনতা দিবস**: Independence Day, **26 March**
- **বিজয় দিবস**: Victory Day, **16 December**

**দিবস** is the formal word for a named 'Day'; everyday 'day' is **দিন**. 'On' and 'to' take **-e**: **স্বাধীনতা দিবসে ছুটি** 'Independence Day is a holiday', **আমরা শহীদ মিনারে যাই** 'we go to the Shaheed Minar'.

alt: The twenty-first of February is Martyrs' Day.

sentences.en: In the morning we go to the Shaheed Minar.
Today is Victory Day, we have a holiday.
alt: It's Victory Day today, so we have the day off.
There is a holiday on Independence Day.

lessons.title: Invitations & guests
lessons.goal: Invite people politely and look after guests.
grammar: future as polite request: আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন 'please come to our home'
lessons.tip:
Bengali invitations use the **future** as a gentle request: **আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন** is literally 'You will come to our home', and it means 'Please do come!' More formally: **আপনাকে দাওয়াত দিলাম** 'I'm inviting you' (lit. 'I gave you an invitation'). To a friend: **তুমি কি আসবে?** 'Will you come?'

Soften it with **যদি** 'if' + the present: **যদি সময় হয়, আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন** 'If you have time, please come'.

A **মেহমান** (guest) is treated with great honour. Expect tea, sweets and **পিঠা** (rice cakes), and expect **খাবেন?** 'Will you have some?' more than once. A first 'no' is often heard as politeness, so accept a little.

**Kolkata:** **নেমন্তন্ন** 'invitation', **অতিথি** 'guest'.

sentences.en: We have guests at home today.
alt: Guests are at our house today.

sentences.bn: যদি সময় হয়, আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন।
sentences.tr: jodi shomoy hoy, amader bashay ashben.
sentences.en: If you have time, please come to our home.
alt: If there is time, please come to our place.

sentences.bn: যখন মেহমান আসে, আমরা চা আর পিঠা খাই।
sentences.tr: jokhon mehman ashe, amra cha ar pitha khai.
sentences.en: When guests come, we have tea and pitha.
alt: When guests come, we eat tea and pitha.

lessons.title: Wishes & gifts
lessons.goal: Wish people well, give a gift and talk about a crowd.
grammar: X-এর জন্য / আপনার জন্য 'for X / for you'
lessons.tip:
Wishes start with **শুভ** 'happy, auspicious': **শুভ জন্মদিন** 'Happy birthday', like **শুভ নববর্ষ**. Festival messages and cards often say **ঈদের শুভেচ্ছা** 'Eid greetings'; to a whole group, **সবাইকে ঈদের শুভেচ্ছা** 'Eid greetings to everyone'. **সবাইকে** is the object form of **সবাই**.

**জন্য** 'for' comes *after* the word, which takes the possessive *-r / -er*: **আপনার জন্য** 'for you', **তোমার জন্য** 'for you (familiar)'. So: **এই উপহার আপনার জন্য** 'This gift is for you'.

A small **উপহার** (gift), such as sweets or fruit, is a nice touch when you visit.

**লোক** is the everyday word for 'people': **মেলায় অনেক লোক** 'There are lots of people at the fair'.

sentences.bn: এই উপহার তোমার জন্য, কারণ আজ তোমার জন্মদিন।
sentences.tr: ei upohar tomar jonno, karon aj tomar jonmodin.
sentences.en: This gift is for you, because today is your birthday.

sentences.bn: আমি তোমার জন্য একটা নতুন বই কিনলাম।
sentences.tr: ami tomar jonno ekta notun boi kinlam.
sentences.en: I bought a new book for you.
There are a lot of people at our home today.
alt: Lots of people are at our house today.

sentences.en: There are a lot of people at the fair.
The gift is very beautiful, thank you.

lessons.title: With close friends
lessons.goal: Use the তুই register naturally with close friends, and suggest 'let's…'.
grammar: 'let's': চল (tui) · চলো (tumi) · চলেন (apni) + present আমি-form: চলো যাই
lessons.tip:
**তুই** is the language of real closeness: best friends, siblings and cousins close in age, and often parents to young children. Among young Bangladeshi friends you'll hear **দোস্ত** ('buddy, mate') all the time. Used with a stranger or someone older, তুই is rude, so only use it with someone your own age (or younger) who already uses it with you. An elder may call you তুই, but you still answer with **আপনি** or **তুমি**.

'Let's…' = **চল / চলো / চলেন** + the আমি-form of the verb. Pick the one that matches the person:

- **চল, মেলায় যাই** — 'Let's go to the fair' (তুই)
- **চলো, যাই** — 'Let's go' (তুমি)
- **চলেন, চা খাই** — 'Shall we have tea?' (আপনি)

The তুই future ends in *-bi*: **আসবি?** 'Will you come?', **কী খাবি?** 'What'll you have?' Compare **আসবে** (তুমি) and **আসবেন** (আপনি) from the last lesson.

**হবে** 'will be / will happen' is the future of 'be': **আজ নাচ আর গান হবে** 'There'll be dancing and singing today'.

**Kolkata:** polite **চলুন** (*cholun*) instead of চলেন; **দোস্ত** is rare there.

sentences.en: There will be dancing and singing today.
alt: Today there will be dance and music.

lessons.title: Review: festivals & friends
lessons.goal: Greet, invite and celebrate across the year, choosing the right register.
grammar: review: festival greetings, -এ for 'at / on / to', invitations with the future, চল/চলো/চলেন, register choice
lessons.tip:
No new words: this review mixes the whole unit.

Match the greeting to the occasion:

- Eid: **ঈদ মোবারক** (in messages also **ঈদের শুভেচ্ছা**)
- Pohela Boishakh: **শুভ নববর্ষ**
- after Durga Puja: **শুভ বিজয়া**
- a birthday: **শুভ জন্মদিন**

Match the register to the person: **চলেন** with your teacher, **চলো** with a classmate, **চল** with your best friend. The future follows the same levels: **আসবেন** · **আসবে** · **আসবি**. When in doubt, go one level *more* polite.

Places and days take **-e**: **ঈদে**, **পূজায়**, **রমজানে**, **মেলায়**, **মন্দিরে**, **শহীদ মিনারে**.

sentences.bn: রমজানে আমরা রোজা রাখি, আর ইফতারে খেজুর খাই।
sentences.tr: romjane amra roja rakhi, ar iftare khejur khai.
sentences.en: In Ramadan we fast, and at iftar we eat dates.
alt: During Ramadan we fast and eat dates at iftar.

sentences.bn: পূজায় আমরা মন্দিরে যাই, আর ঈদে আমরা গ্রামে যাই।
sentences.tr: pujay amra mondire jai, ar ide amra grame jai.
sentences.en: At Puja we go to the temple, and at Eid we go to the village.

sentences.bn: একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি আমরা শহীদ মিনারে যাই।
sentences.tr: ekushe februari amra shohid minare jai.
sentences.en: On 21 February we go to the Shaheed Minar.

sentences.bn: আজ পহেলা বৈশাখ, চলো মেলায় যাই।
sentences.tr: aj pohela boishakh, cholo melay jai.
sentences.en: Today is Pohela Boishakh, let's go to the fair.

sentences.bn: যদি সময় হয়, আমাদের বাসায় আসবেন, পিঠা খাবেন।
sentences.tr: jodi shomoy hoy, amader bashay ashben, pitha khaben.
sentences.en: If you have time, please come to our home and have some pitha.
There will be dancing and singing today.
